# Tobit Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** Now Tobit his-father was counting each day, and when the days-of the-journey were-fulfilled and they had not come, Tobit said,

**10:2** "Perhaps he has been detained there? Or perhaps Gabael has died and there is no one to give him the money?"

**10:3** And he was grieved in-soul. And his-wife Anna said, "The boy has perished; he is no-longer among the living." And she began to weep and to-wail over her son,

**10:4** saying, "O woe to-me, child, that I let you go — you, the light-of my eyes!"

**10:5** And Tobit said to-her, "Be-silent! Do not be troubled; he is well."

**10:6** And she said to-him, "Be-silent yourself! Do not deceive me. My child has perished." And she went out every-day onto the-road on which he had gone and looked by day, and ceased [only] when she ate; at-night she did not cease wailing [for] the Tobias her-son.

**10:7** Now the fourteen days-of the-wedding had-passed, which Raguel had-sworn for-his-daughter. And Tobias came to-him and said, "Send me, for I know that my father and my mother no-longer believe [that] they will see me. And now I beg you, father, let me depart so-that I may go to my father; I have already told you how I left him."

**10:8** And Raguel said to-Tobias, "Remain with me and I will send [word] to your father, and they will tell him how-you-are." And Tobias said, "Not-so; I beg you, send me to my father."

**10:9** And Raguel rose and gave to-him Sarah his-wife, and the half-of all-his-goods: male-slaves and female-slaves, and cattle and donkeys and sheep, and clothing and money and furnishings.

**10:10** And he sent them-away safe-and-sound, and he embraced Tobias and said to-him, "Farewell, child; have a safe-journey. May the-Lord-of heaven grant you and Sarah your-wife well-being, and may I see your children before I die."

**10:11** And he said to Sarah his-daughter, "Go to your father-in-law; from now-on they are your parents as those who begot you. Go in-peace, daughter; may I hear good-report of you as-long-as I live." And he kissed her and sent-her-away.

**10:12** And Edna said to Tobias, "Child — beloved-brother — may the-Lord bring you back and may I see your children-of Sarah my-daughter before I die; in-the-sight-of the-Lord I entrust my-daughter to-you. Do not cause-her-grief all the days-of your-life. Go in-peace, child. From now on I am your mother and Sarah [is] your sister. May we prosper together all the-days-of our-lives." And she kissed him.

**10:13** And Tobias departed from Raguel in-good-health and-joy, blessing the-Lord-of heaven and earth, the-King-of all, because he had-made-prosper his journey. And he said to-him, "Be-it-granted to-you to honor your parents all the-days-of your-lives, and to accomplish-the-will-of Edna your-mother-in-law." [And he departed with-them being-blessed until they were-near to Nineveh.]

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

- **10:1**: "Counting each day" — the Greek hemeran par' hemeran is literally "day by day/each day beside the next"; EMET preserves the iterative sense.
- **10:3**: Anna's grief is rendered with its two Greek verbs: klaio (weep) and threnos (wail/lament). The distinction matters — wailing is public, grief-ritual language.
- **10:4**: "Light of my eyes" — idiomatic Greek for a cherished child; preserved as it is also biblical Hebrew idiom (Ps 38:10, Prov 7:2).
- **10:6**: The detail that Anna "ceased [only] when she ate" is GII-specific and psychologically precise. It is kept in full.
- **10:9**: The list of goods is rendered item by item — oiketai, paidiskai, boes, onoi, probata, himatia, argyrion, skeue. EMET renders all: male-slaves, female-slaves, cattle, donkeys, sheep, clothing, money, furnishings.
- **10:13**: The bracketed final clause is present in Sinaiticus but may be a scribal addition or transition marker.

*— EMET*
